LESSON: TYPES OF DIVORCE • AT-TALAQ • KHUL’U

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: General
Strand: Muamalat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.2: Types of divorce • at-Talaq • khul’u
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Types of divorce • at-Talaq • khul’u, part of Muamalat (Social Relations) in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 General.

Key inquiry question: How does talaq affect families? 2. Why is khul’u common in families?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. research on at-Talaq and Khul’u types of divorce and make a class presentation,

2. discuss the steps involved in at- Talaq and Khul’u according to Islamic teachings in groups and present on charts/power points,

3. listen to a resource person (kadhi/imam) giving a talk on the steps involved in at-Talaq and Khul’u,

4. research on the effects of divorce and make notes. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. research on at-Talaq and Khul’u types of divorce and make a class presentation,
2. discuss the steps involved in at- Talaq and Khul’u according to Islamic teachings in groups and present on charts/power points,
3. listen to a resource person (kadhi/imam) giving a talk on the steps involved in at-Talaq and Khul’u,
4. research on the effects of divorce and make notes. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Types of divorce • at-Talaq • khul’u together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: enhanced as learners learn independently through listening to a resource person (kadhi/imam) on

the steps involved in at-Talaq and Khul’u.

• Communication and collaboration: enhanced as learners speak effectively and engagingly when discussing the

steps involved in at-Talaq and Khul’u.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of interpretation and inferences enhanced as learners listen to a

resource person (kadhi/imam) on the steps involved in at-Talaq and Khul’u.

Values:
Social justice is enhanced as learners discuss the steps involved in at-Talaq and Khul’u.
